summary: Bitoku is a dense hand-management and worker-placement engine-builder where you send dice-workers into forest regions to unlock actions, build structures, and grow a hand of yōkai cards that combo together; turns are short but each one matters, and the tableau grows into a satisfying engine over the game's two hours. It rewards planning a route through several scoring paths (structures, crystals, mitama tracks, set collection) rather than one dominant strategy.
praised: Rich, tightly interlocking engine-building with a strong sense of progression each round
Beautiful, thematic art and production quality
Multiple viable paths to victory that reward long-term planning
criticised: Steep rules overhead and long first-play teach relative to the payoff
Significant analysis paralysis, especially with 4 players
Iconography-heavy cards can be hard to parse early on
Player interaction is fairly limited/indirect for a 120-minute game

interaction.kind: area denial on worker placement spots, mostly parallel engine-building

scoring.why: Final score is an accumulation across structures, crystals, mitamas, sets, and end-game bonuses, so efficient engine-building across several tracks decides the winner rather than any single dominant path
